chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, by his chain, from one of them (peace be upon him), regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Surely the rising by night is the firmest way to tread and the best speech.'

He (peace be upon him) said: 'These are two Rak'at after Al-Maghrib. You should recite in the first Rak'at with the Opening of the Book, and ten verses from the beginning of Al-Baqarah, and the Verse of Al-Sakhra, and from His Words: "And your God is one God! There is no god but He; He is the Beneficent, the Merciful. Surely in the Creation of the skies and the earth..." up to His Words: "...there are signs for a people who understand." And fifteen times: Say, He is Allah, One.'"

And in the second Rak'at, the Opening of the Book, and the Verse of the Throne, and the end of Al-Baqarah, from His Words: "To Allah belongs whatever is in the skies and whatever is in the earth," up to the end of the Chapter. And fifteen times: Say, He is Allah, One. Then, after this, supplicate with whatever you desire.'
He (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who persevered upon it, there would be written for him, with each Salat, six hundred thousand performances of Hajj.'

key_terms.آيَةَ الْكُرْسِيِّ: The Verse of the Throne (Ayat al-Kursi)
key_terms.فَاتِحَةِ الْكِتَابِ: The Opening of the Book (Surah Al-Fatiha)
key_terms.قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ: Say, He is Allah, One (Surah Al-Ikhlas)
key_terms.ناشِئَةَ اللَّيْلِ: Rising by night (referring to night prayer)
key_terms.وَاظَبَ عَلَيْهِ: Persevered upon it / was consistent with it

ai.seo_question: What are the specific Quranic recitations and rewards for the two-Rak'at night prayer after Maghrib?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* elucidates the specific recitation protocol for the two-Rak'at night prayer (Salat al-Layl) following Maghrib, linking the practice to the Quranic verse 'Inna nash'ata al-layl' (73:6) as a means of spiritual clarity. It prescribes a unique combination of Surahs and verses for each Rak'ah, culminating in a personal supplication, and highlights the immense reward of six hundred thousand Hajj performances for consistent adherence. This narration is often cited in Shia tradition to emphasize the merit of night worship and the specific devotional practices associated with the Ahl al-Bayt.
